page: Amazon Web Services c5d.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It includes 100 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c5d.xlarge mostly in the lower performance tiers. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, fall into the bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests, such as PassMark memory score and large-block read/write operations, rank as weak or poor, with large-block read-only bandwidth at 26.2 GB/sec. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 24.03 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 9.13 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c5d.xlarge pairs dedicated compute resources with high-speed local NVMe storage, making it suitable for workloads requiring low-latency scratch space without the overhead of network-attached storage. However, the tradeoff lies in its lower overall processing and memory bandwidth scores relative to newer hardware generations. This instance is configured for workloads such as basic web serving, light batch processing, single-threaded compression tasks, and development environments requiring local temporary storage.
